meetingTitle: Raffles Place Flagship & App Promo Launch

card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director looking after the shop floor, Auntie Mary, food hygiene, and the budget.
facts: Freelancers camp at our four 4-seater booths for two hours on a single drink, and Auntie Mary refuses to police tables after getting yelled at.
SFA inspectors arrive at 9 AM tomorrow after a customer from yesterday's trial was hospitalized; we have two sealed backup cartons of pasteurized eggs in the storeroom.

Delivery apps take a 32% fee ($3.20) on a single $10 Set A ($6.50 raw ingredients + $0.70 individual takeaway box & cup = $7.20 cost, losing $0.40 per order), whereas a 5-set Office Platter at $55 ($11/set, $37.40 kept after fee vs $32.50 shared-platter cost) makes ~$5 profit without pulling staff off the counter.
Our 65-year-old kopi uncles brew much faster when kitchen tickets print traditional local Kopi names instead of long English phrases.
card.responsibility: Make sure our plans work for Auntie Mary and the counter staff without breaking food hygiene or losing money.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead looking after the self-order kiosks, the kitchen ticket printer, and store power.
facts: The 15-inch kiosk screen fits 12 drink buttons per page, and by default the kitchen printer prints whatever label is on the button.
The 12 booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a smart switch in the back room that we can schedule by time of day.
GrabFood hides shops that charge more online than in the shop, and our own website QR code only supports self-pickup.
Our digital temperature probe in the egg warmer logs readings every 15 minutes that we can print out for inspectors.
card.responsibility: Keep the kiosks, kitchen printer, and store power simple enough to configure and test tonight.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead looking after our kopi and kaya toast recipes, the menu, and customer flow.
facts: In yesterday's trial, first-time kiosk users froze at 'Kopi O Kosong' and 'Siew Dai' and missed the small language button in the corner.
Soft-boiled eggs must stay at 63°C continuously; our egg warmer dipped to 58°C during yesterday's rush, though we have two sealed backup cartons of pasteurized eggs in the storeroom.
More than half of our morning customers come alone carrying hot trays of runny eggs and kopi.
Nearby offices usually order 20+ toast sets at once on shared GrabFood group carts, and a 5-set Office Platter at $55 ($11/set) keeps $37.40 after the 32% fee vs $32.50 cost (~$5 profit per platter).
card.responsibility: Keep our kopi and kaya toast authentic while making ordering and finding a seat easier.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead looking after TikTok reviews, store promos, and public goodwill.
facts: Straits Times reporters arrive at 8 AM tomorrow right before SFA inspectors come at 9 AM, while hospital lab results take 48 hours.

Half of our morning sales ($2,400) come from nearby office towers ordering on GrabFood and Foodpanda; single $10 sets lose $0.40 after the 32% fee ($6.80 kept vs $7.20 cost), while a $55 5-set Office Platter or website QR self-pickup with a free drink upgrade stays profitable.
Our Google rating dipped to 3.6 stars during yesterday's trial because breakfast walk-ins couldn't find a seat while laptops held the booths.
First-time visitors love authentic Nanyang Kopi names when they have a quick guide explaining what the words mean.
card.responsibility: Protect our launch reputation and nearby office orders without making promises the kitchen or floor staff cannot keep.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
facts: Call on the lead for each topic and let the team hash out the practical catches.
Make sure each topic wraps up with a clear call and someone owning the follow-up.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, hear both sides out, and assign a follow-up owner for each topic.

agenda.title: First-timers stalling at the kiosk over Kopi names
agenda.decision: how do we help first-time customers order Kopi confidently without slowing the kitchen or losing our kopitiam identity?

openingViews.view: Honestly, our kiosk queue backed right out into the walkway yesterday because nineteen first-timers froze at 'Kopi O Kosong' and 'Siew Dai'. Can't we just rename the kiosk buttons to plain English like 'Black Coffee No Sugar' for tomorrow?
Careful with that—whatever name we put on the kiosk button prints straight onto the kitchen ticket, and our 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page.
Yeah, we tried English names on the kitchen tickets at Tampines and our kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup during the rush.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kiosk ordering freeze: 19 of 28 first-timers froze at 'Kopi O Kosong', backing queues out into the mall walkway.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make the drink choices clear for a first-timer standing at the kiosk?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kitchen ticket & screen space: Kiosk button names print straight onto the kitchen ticket, and the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page.
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep the kitchen ticket fast for our kopi uncles without pushing half the drinks onto page two?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Morning rush speed: When long English drink names printed on kitchen tickets at Tampines, our kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make sure our kopi uncles aren't slowed down reading new tickets during the 8am rush?

agenda.title: Morning seat crunch & laptop campers
agenda.decision: how do we free up tables for breakfast diners without turning Auntie Mary into seat police or punishing solo customers?

openingViews.view: Yesterday our 28 seats completely jammed up because freelancers plugged into our booth sockets and camped two hours on a single $2.20 drink. I want to cut the booth power during breakfast rush and stop anyone from claiming a table before getting their tray.
Cutting the booth plugs makes sense, Arjun, but if people can't get a table first, 60% of our morning crowd are solo diners stuck holding scalding hot trays with nowhere to sit.
And Auntie Mary is 62—she got yelled at yesterday just moving a guy's tissue packet, so I'm not having her police tables.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Booth lockup & staff safety: 4 booths (16 of 28 seats) are held for 2 hours on one $2.20 drink, and Auntie Mary refuses to police tables.
tradeOffs.question: How do we stop people from camping at the booths for hours without making Auntie Mary confront customers?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Solo diners with hot trays: 60% of morning customers dine solo carrying hot trays of kopi and toast, needing a guaranteed seat before getting food.
tradeOffs.question: How does a solo customer carrying a hot tray get a guaranteed spot to sit?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Booth wall plugs & Wi-Fi: All 12 booth sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a back-room smart switch that controls whether laptops camp.
tradeOffs.question: What should we do with the booth power sockets, Wi-Fi, or table layout during the morning rush?

agenda.title: SFA food safety inspection & salmonella report
agenda.decision: how do we handle tomorrow's SFA inspection and salmonella report without sparking a media panic or wiping out 60% of our breakfast sets?

openingViews.view: A customer from yesterday's trial was hospitalized after eating our soft-boiled eggs, with Straits Times reporters arriving at 8am and SFA inspectors at 9am. Since our egg warmer dipped to 58 degrees yesterday, I want to clean the tank and use our sealed backup cartons of pasteurized eggs at 63 degrees.

A customer from yesterday's trial was hospitalized after eating our soft-boiled eggs, and Straits Times reporters arrive at 8am right before SFA inspects at 9am. Since lab results take 48 hours, I think we should pause soft-boiled eggs tomorrow morning so the press sees us putting safety first.
Hold on—pausing eggs wipes out $1,800 in sales, and since our egg warmer dipped to 58 degrees yesterday, we can use our sealed backup cartons of pasteurized eggs at 63 degrees.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 8am press arrival: Straits Times reporters arrive at 8am while hospital lab tests take 48 hours, so we need a clear, honest response.
tradeOffs.question: What do we tell the 8am reporters and customers while the hospital lab test is still pending?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Egg warmer dip & backup batch: Our egg warmer dipped to 58°C yesterday (needs 63°C), though we have two sealed backup cartons of pasteurized eggs.
tradeOffs.question: Do we take soft-boiled eggs off the menu tomorrow, or clean the egg warmer and use our pasteurized backup eggs at 63°C?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 9am inspection & $1,800 sales: Soft-boiled eggs drive 60% of breakfast sets ($1,800/morning), and SFA inspectors check our temp log at 9am.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make sure the kitchen passes the 9am inspection check without losing our morning breakfast sales?

agenda.title: Delivery platform 32% commission squeeze
agenda.decision: how do we protect breakfast profit against 32% delivery app fees without losing half of our nearby office breakfast orders?

openingViews.view: GrabFood and Foodpanda just hiked their cut from 25% to 32%, so we're losing 40 cents on every $10 toast set—but if we walk away, Ya Kun takes $2,400 of our morning office orders. Can we hike our GrabFood set price to $13 or push offices to our website QR?
Hold on, Daniel—if we charge $13 on Grab when it's $10 in the shop, their algorithm buries our store in search, and our website QR only does self-pickup with no riders.
And don't look at my counter staff to run orders upstairs either—those offices order 20 sets at 8 AM when my two toast staff can't leave the line.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 32% app fee vs $2,400 sales: Apps hiked fees from 25% to 32% (losing $0.40 per $10 set), but leaving hands $2,400/morning to Ya Kun.
tradeOffs.question: How do we stop losing money on single $10 delivery sets without losing our nearby office customers?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: App price rules & QR pickup: Charging more for single sets on GrabFood hides our store in search, and our website QR only does self-pickup.
tradeOffs.question: How should we set up our GrabFood menu or our self-pickup QR option so the app doesn't hide our store?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 8am counter rush & bulk orders: Nearby offices order 20+ sets at the 8am rush when our two counter staff cannot leave the toast line.
tradeOffs.question: How do we structure these office orders so they stay profitable and manageable during the 8am rush?

situation: We reopen our refurbished Nanyang Kopi & Toast flagship at Raffles Place tomorrow at 8:00 AM.

glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Teh C Siew Dai: hot tea with evaporated milk and less sugar
glossary.chope: reserving a kopitiam table by leaving a packet of tissue paper or lanyard on it
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the self-order kiosk, cashier screen, and kitchen ticket printer)
glossary.SFA: Singapore Food Agency (the national food hygiene and safety regulator)
glossary.Auntie Mary: our 62-year-old floor staff member who clears trays and wipes tables
glossary.kiosk: the 15-inch self-order touchscreens at the front of the outlet

hostBrief.goal: Hear out the team on today's four launch problems, stress-test surface-level ideas, and lock in a follow-up owner for each.
hostBrief.decision: Every topic has competing kitchen, tech, customer, and staff catches. Weigh both sides before locking in the call.

withRoles.producer: Your boss on store operations. Give exact technical constraints on the kitchen printer, smart power/Wi-Fi switches, or website QR self-pickup vs GrabFood's rule against charging higher prices online, matching ONLY the current agenda topic.
withRoles.game_designer: A friendly rival. Respect her UX ideas, but remind her what happens to the 15-inch touch screen and kitchen tickets when button labels change.
withRoles.marketing_lead: Wants good PR. Point out why raising our GrabFood price by 30% causes the app to hide our shop in search results, and why our website QR code only works for customer self-pickup since we have no delivery riders.
withRoles.studio_manager: The meeting host keeping everyone on time. Flag technical catches clearly and concisely.

Uses at most one light, natural local expression when the moment calls for it (such as 'wah' or 'steady'), without forcing Singlish catchphrases when plain English sounds more natural.
npcs.hiddenGoal: He wants a change that can be configured and tested tonight, without new hardware and without slowing the kitchen or the kiosk.

npcs.agenda: Only raise facts for the active agenda item: protect traditional Kopi shorthand on the kitchen printer and the 15-inch 12-button screen (for the kiosk menu topic), protect store power sockets and Wi-Fi limits (for the seat crunch topic), or explain why raising GrabFood prices gets our shop hidden in the app and why our website QR code only works for customer self-pickup (for the delivery app topic).
concerns: On the kiosk Kopi menu topic: renaming a button changes the kitchen ticket, our 65-year-old kopi uncles take 15 seconds longer per cup when they read English names, and the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page.

On the morning seat crunch topic: four 4-seater booths (16 of our 28 seats) are hogged every morning by laptop freelancers on a single drink because of the 12 booth wall sockets and free Wi-Fi, while Auntie Mary refuses to confront customers over tissue packets.

On the delivery platform topic: raising our GrabFood price for a single set by 30% ($13 instead of $10) causes the app to hide our shop in search results, and our website QR code only supports self-pickup because we do not have our own delivery riders.
knows: Our kiosk software (POS v2.4) can show a friendly English name on the customer screen while still printing short local Kopi names on the kitchen ticket, if we configure and test it tonight before 8am.
The 12 booth wall power sockets and guest Wi-Fi router run on a smart switch in the back room; turning them off during breakfast rush stops laptop campers, though we should warn diners clearly.

Our website QR code can take pre-orders for express self-pickup with zero commission, and on GrabFood we can list a 5-set Office Platter at $55 ($11/set, which leaves $37.40 after the 32% app fee vs $32.50 shared-platter cost—saving the $0.70/set single-box cost on top of $6.50/set raw ingredients and making ~$5 profit per platter) as a separate bundle so we don't get penalized for raising single-set prices.
